Coset codes extend traditional cyclic structures by embedding redundancy that compensates for misframing events, effectively creating equivalence classes that maintain integrity even when synchronization is lost. Subset codes refine this approach by selecting specific codewords that form a coherent substructure, enabling more efficient decoding strategies. These primitives are mathematically unified through finite field theory and group actions on code spaces. The failure mode occurs when either the number of frame errors exceeds the designed tolerance or when decoding algorithms cannot resolve ambiguities introduced by overlapping cosets. Dualities emerge between the structure of these codes and their corresponding syndrome spaces, where each coset corresponds to a distinct error pattern. In GSI, these are modeled as probabilistic belief updates conditioned on observed syndromes. In GSE, they define deterministic state transitions within a decoding automaton.
